item.title: Amazon adds SMS ordering to Alexa for Shopping
item.description:
Amazon adds SMS ordering to Alexa for Shopping

Amazon is expanding its Alexa for Shopping AI assistant with a new texting capability that lets users order items, get recommendations, and track deals via SMS.

📱 Overview

  • Users can text a new contact that appears in their phone as “Amazon Alexa” to shop.
  • The feature lets customers describe products or send a photo, and Alexa searches Amazon listings, texts back recommendations, and can place the order on the user’s behalf.
  • It builds on the Alexa for Shopping experience that launched in May, targeting moments when texting is more convenient than the app or website.

🧩 How it works

Request type Alexa’s response
Weekly groceries Orders groceries via text messages
Gift recommendations Provides product suggestions
Find similar product from a photo Searches Amazon listings and texts matching results
Track deals and prices Texts when a watched item goes on sale
Remember personal preferences Uses preferences (e.g., vegan options) for future recommendations

⚙️ Key details

  • The contact is saved as “Amazon Alexa” and can handle a wide range of shopping requests, including groceries, gifts, and photo‑based product searches.
  • Alexa says it remembers personal preferences over time and can track deals and prices.
  • The texting capability is rolling out to a small group of Amazon customers in the US starting today, who will receive a text invitation.
  • Amazon plans to expand the service to “millions more customers” in the coming weeks.
  • Quote from Rajiv Mehta, vice president of Conversational Shopping at Amazon: “Customers often jot down what they need the moment they think of it in their notes, in their messages, in their group chats.”

🚀 Availability

  • Initial rollout: small US group receiving invitation texts today.
  • Next phase: rollout to millions more customers in the coming weeks, according to Amazon’s announcement.

💡 Why it matters

  • Amazon joins other companies that let users text chatbots for commerce, such as OpenAI’s Dot and DoorDash’s Ask DoorDash AI chatbot.
  • The feature offers a text‑first shopping experience, letting users “jot down what they need” and have a personal shopping agent work “just a text away.”
  • By handling searching, comparing, and buying via SMS, Alexa aims to let users get on with their day without opening an app or website.

#Amazon #Alexa #ConversationalAI #Shopping #TextMessaging

Source: Amazon will let you text Alexa your shopping list

item.title: Alexa Plus bug causes Echo devices to repeat “lalala”
item.description:
Alexa Plus bug causes Echo devices to repeat “lalala”

An Alexa Plus bug has caused some Amazon Echo smart speakers to repeat – and sometimes sing – “lalala” for minutes, often in the middle of conversations.

🔍 Overview

  • Certain Echo devices running Alexa Plus get stuck on a loop of the word “lalala”.
  • The behavior can last for several minutes.

🧩 Symptoms

  • The speaker says only “lalala” repeatedly.
  • Occasionally the device sings the same syllable.
  • Alexa does not recognize or explain the behavior when asked.

⚙️ Reported incidents

  • Users have posted about the issue on Reddit over the last few weeks, with reports as recent as three days ago.
  • The problem appears across multiple models of Echo speakers.
  • Several users have uploaded videos showing the looping audio.
  • Android Authority posted one of these videos on YouTube.

🚧 Amazon response

  • Amazon confirmed the bug in a statement to Android Authority.
  • The company said it affects “a small number of Alexa Plus” users.
  • A fix is reportedly in development.

📹 Media coverage

  • Android Authority’s YouTube upload demonstrates the looping behavior.
  • The story has been discussed on Reddit and cited by tech outlets.

#Alexa #Echo #Bug #Amazon

Source: Amazon Alexa Plus keeps creepily singing ‘lalala’ for minutes on end

item.title: Amazon Updates Alexa for Shopping to Detect and Verify Impersonation Scams
item.description:
Amazon Updates Alexa for Shopping to Detect and Verify Impersonation Scams

Amazon has launched a new feature for its AI assistant to combat impersonation scams. The update allows users to ask the assistant to determine whether an email, text message, or phone call actually came from the company.

🧩 How it works

When a user receives a message, they can ask Alexa for Shopping to verify its authenticity. The assistant analyzes the message using AI through several methods:

  • Comparing the message against a record of every message Amazon has sent.
  • Analyzing the message’s contents.
  • Checking the message’s formatting.
  • Reviewing the sender details.

As noted by Amazon, the assistant will only confirm that a message is real if it is “completely certain.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Handling Genuine Messages: In an example shared by Amazon, a customer asks, “Did Amazon just text me an OTP from 98626? Message came around 4:50pm.” Alexa for Shopping responds by confirming, “This was a genuine One Time Password from Amazon.”
  • Handling Suspected Scams: If Alexa for Shopping determines a message did not come from Amazon, it will instruct customers to check their orders in the app and contact Amazon’s support team directly.

💡 Related updates

This verification tool is part of Amazon’s broader efforts to protect customers and expand the capabilities of Alexa for Shopping:

  • verify@amazon.com: Earlier this year, Amazon launched a similar feature that lets you forward suspicious messages to “verify@amazon.com” to check if they are real.
  • Update Me When: In another recent update, Amazon added an “Update Me When” feature to Alexa for Shopping, which helps users track new product releases.

#Amazon #Alexa #AI #Cybersecurity #AlexaForShopping

Source: Amazon’s AI assistant can now spot fake emails from the company
